newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-PRASAD TAKES 5-60 AS SOUTH AFRICA STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PRASAD TAKES 5-60 AS SOUTH AFRICA STRUGGLE.

text.p: Seamer Venkatesh Prasad captured five for 60 as India seized the initiative against South Africa on the opening day of the first test at Kingsmead on Thursday.
By the close, India were two without loss in reply to South Africa's first innings of 235 all out, the substance of which was a fluent 80 from opener Andrew Hudson.

Hudson, initially shaky against the swinging ball, posted his 11th test 50 and struck 12 fours before being caught behind by wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia off the gentle seam of Saurav Ganguly. Mongia finished with five catches in the innings.
The Indian attack, spearheaded by the accurate Javagal Srinath with two for 36, dominated for much of the day after the home side were invited to bat first in hot, humid conditions.

Although South Africa recovered well during the morning session after the early loss of opener Gary Kirsten for two, they then slid from 70 for one at lunch to 113 for five by the 44th over on a relatively blameless pitch.
The 23-year-old number three batsman Adam Bacher, on his test debut, had given Hudson solid support during the first session with a composed 25.
Yet it was only much later in the day that all-rounders Brian McMillan (34) and Shaun Pollock (23 not out), as well as wicketkeeper Dave Richardson (24), provided further South African resistance.
Bacher, who had played without blemish during a partnership of 62 for the second wicket with Hudson, departed two overs after lunch.
Playing half forward defensively, he was adjudged leg before to a Srinath off-cutter, having faced 73 deliveries and struck three fours and a hooked six.

The only other partnership of any substance was 49 for the sixth wicket between Hudson and McMillan. After the departure of McMillan, leg before to the seam of David Johnson, the rest of the South African innings fell away in a further 11 overs.
Prasad claimed the final scalp of Allan Donald, caught by Vikram Rathore at third slip, to register his third haul of five wickets or more in a test ininngs.

Hudson said: "It's the sort of wicket where you need a bit of luck -- and I was just fortunate that it went my way. But you're never really in on this sort of wicket and the Indian attack bowled better after lunch, getting the right line and length.
"The pitch has got quite a steep bounce and it's swung more than it has seamed today...and that combination of swing and bounce has been our undoing."
